title: Next.js Image Component
description: Optimise images automatically – lazy loading, responsive sizes, and modern formats.

slides.title: The `` Tag is Slow 🐢
slides.content:
# Image Problems

* Huge file sizes slow down your page.
* No built‑in lazy loading (before loading="lazy").
* Layout shift – image loads late and pushes content down.
* Not optimised for different screen sizes.

Next.js provides a **`next/image`** component that solves all this automatically.

```jsx
import Image from 'next/image';

<Image src="/profile.jpg" width={200} height={200} alt="User" />
```

slides.title: Using next/image (pages/index.js)
slides.content: Always provide `width`, `height`, and `alt`. The image will be lazy‑loaded and responsive by default.

quizData.question: Why must you provide `width` and `height` to the Next.js Image component?

options.text: For the browser to scale the image
To prevent layout shift by reserving the space before the image loads
It's optional; you don't need them

quizData.explanation: Next.js uses the given dimensions to calculate the aspect ratio and allocate the correct space, eliminating Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).

slides.title: Priority & Loading 🚨
slides.content:
# Above‑the‑Fold Images

For your main hero image, add the `priority` prop. It tells Next.js to preload the image and skip lazy loading.

```jsx
<Image src="/hero.jpg" width={1200} height={600} priority />
```

Without `priority`, all images lazy‑load by default. Use it only for the largest contentful paint (LCP) image.

`loading="eager"` is also available but `priority` also adds `fetchPriority="high"`.

slides.title: External Images (next.config.js)
slides.content: To use images from a remote URL, you must whitelist the domain in `next.config.js`.

quizData.question: What happens if you use `<Image src="https://unsplash.com/photo.jpg">` without configuring the domain?

options.text: Next.js throws an error during development and the image won't be optimized

quizData.explanation: For security and performance, Next.js requires you to explicitly allow external image sources in `next.config.js`.

slides.title: Responsive Sizes & fill 🔄
slides.content:
# Flexible Images If you don't know the dimensions (e.g., for a full‑width image), use the `fill` prop. ```jsx
``` `fill` makes the image fill its parent container. You must set the parent to `position: relative`. For responsive images with `srcset`, you can use `sizes` prop.

slides.title: Performance Gold 🏆
slides.content: Images are served in modern WebP format automatically when supported. They are also cached on Vercel's edge network. Always use `next/image` unless you really need a simple ``.
